_purpose: Which physical camera plays which role, and how to open it. Matched by identity (VID:PID / serial), never by /dev/video number — those get reshuffled on every boot.

_hardware_found._note: The two C920s report the SAME product name but DIFFERENT product IDs (08e5 vs 0892), so VID:PID alone tells them apart. No USB-port pinning needed — these cables can move freely.

_bandwidth.problem: All three cameras sit on ONE USB 2.0 hub (bus 001, 480 Mbps shared). Uncompressed YUYV 640x480@30 reserves ~18 MB/s PER C920; add the ZED's ~15 MB/s and the bus is over budget. That is why /dev/video2 threw select() timeouts and every feed collapsed to under 1 fps.
_bandwidth.fix: fourcc MJPG on both C920s below — compressed, ~1-2 MB/s each instead of 18. The ZED offers only YUYV so it cannot be compressed; it gets the headroom instead.
_bandwidth.even_better: Move the ZED to a USB 3 port on a different controller. Its port path changes from 1-... to 2-..., or the speed field in camera_probe.py jumps from 480 to 5000. Nothing in this file needs to change when you do — that is the point of matching on VID:PID.

intake._camera: ZED 2 stereo — the main bean intake camera
intake._why: only 2b03:f780 device on the machine; 2b03:f781 is its HID interface and has no video node
intake._mac: on a Mac there is no VID:PID matching, so the debug tools resolve this role by name instead
intake._modes: this camera offers exactly one: YUYV 1344x376 @ 15 fps

separator._camera: Logitech C920 (older revision, no serial) over the separator chute
separator._why: pid 08e5 is unique to this unit
separator._mac: on a Mac there is no VID:PID matching, so the debug tools resolve this role by name instead

benefits._camera: Logitech C920 (newer revision, serial 0E9612EF) looking at the benefit boxes
benefits._why: matched on serial as well as pid — the strongest match available
benefits._mac: on a Mac there is no VID:PID matching, so the debug tools resolve this role by name instead
